overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law on notices, executive session procedure, contract votes, roll calls and minutes, declined to nullify the contract votes, and ordered member training.

allegations.summary: Ten executive session notices listed only 'Contract Negotiations' without the counterparty or the executive session purpose relied on.
allegations.key_passage: The topic, "Executive Session; Contract Negotiations," failed to inform the public with whom the Board was negotiating or under which of the permissible executive session purposes.

allegations.summary: The April 19, 2013 notice omitted any open session, though the Board voted in open session before going into executive session.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the notice for the Board's April 19, 2013 executive session meeting was insufficient because it did not indicate that there would be an open session prior to the executive session on that date.

allegations.summary: The June 4, 2013 notice did not list Open Meeting Law complaints, which the chair anticipated discussing at least 48 hours ahead.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the Board failed to list all reasonably anticipated topics for discussion in the notice for its June 4, 2013 meeting.

allegations.summary: The July 1, 2013 agenda item 'Discuss/vote regarding open meeting law complaints' was alleged to be too vague to signal a vote to ratify contracts.
allegations.key_passage: it was reasonably inferable that a "vote regarding open meeting law complaints" could include a vote to ratify those agreements.

allegations.summary: A landscaping issue raised by the Town Administrator in open session was discussed and voted on although not on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Board could properly discuss the topic even though it was not listed on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: The chair's verbal statement before entering executive session, 'regarding contract negotiations', was alleged to be too vague.
allegations.key_passage: we also find its verbal statement that the Board would enter executive session "regarding contract negotiations" was not sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: The chair did not declare that an open meeting may harm the bargaining position before executive sessions on the dispatchers' union contract.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair failed to make such a statement prior to the executive session meetings during which the Board discussed the Dispatchers' contract.

allegations.summary: No declaration was required for non-union contract discussions, so the alleged omission of a Purpose 3 declaration for them was not a violation.
allegations.key_passage: thus its failure to do so did not violate the law as Mr. Pape alleges.

allegations.summary: Alleged failure to disclose in open session that a contract was expiring before going into executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board did not violate the law by failing to do so.

allegations.summary: The chair did not publicly announce whether open session would reconvene after the executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: The Board's minutes do not indicate whether the Chair stated if the Board would reconvene in open session after the executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Two contracts were discussed within a single executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Public bodies may discuss multiple topics and multiple contracts within a single executive session, provided all are appropriate for executive session, are sufficiently noticed, and the appropriate procedures are followed to enter into executive session.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the executive session discussions of the Town Administrator and Police Chief contracts did not fit any permitted purpose.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the discussions that occurred were appropriate for executive session because they fit within Purposes 2 and 3.

allegations.summary: Discussion of the Town Administrator's professional competence in executive session was alleged to be a prohibited clandestine performance review.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore do not find this to be the type of clandestine performance review prohibited by law.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the discussion improperly concerned disciplinary action and character under Purpose 1 without notice to the Town Administrator.
allegations.key_passage: As the subjects discussed were appropriate under Purpose 2, we find it unnecessary to consider whether they might have been appropriate under other executive session purposes.

allegations.summary: The Board voted in executive session to execute the Town Administrator and Police Chief contracts and signed them behind closed doors; ratification in open session was insufficient.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board had authority under Purpose 2 to strategize and negotiate with the Town Administrator and the Police Chief in executive session, the Board violated the law by voting to execute and signing these two contracts behind closed doors.

allegations.summary: Executive session votes were recorded as 'All in favor' rather than by roll call.
allegations.key_passage: This means that, to ensure a clear record of deliberations conducted outside of the public view, even votes with a unanimous outcome must be recorded by roll call.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes referred to documents and contract proposals that were not listed in the minutes.
allegations.key_passage: In multiple instances, the Board's executive session minutes reference the use of documents or exhibits that are not listed in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Alleged that minutes did not show which contracts were discussed or voted on.
allegations.key_passage: We disagree, and find the minutes were sufficient in this regard.

allegations.summary: Alleged that executive session minutes were inaccurate because they contradicted the chair's statements at Town Meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Mr. Pape's allegation relates more to the truthfulness of Chairman Sushchyk's statements during the Town Meeting than the accuracy of these particular meeting minutes, thus we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the March 27 and April 11, 2013 executive session minutes were not approved before release.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find no violation of the Open Meeting Law, but remind the Board that minutes must include a record of all the decisions made and the actions taken at each meeting, including a record of all votes.

allegations.summary: Alleged that executive session minutes were withheld until publicly released on May 23, 2013; the AG issued a reminder without deciding withholding.
allegations.key_passage: Regardless, we remind the Board that a public body must release executive session minutes

allegations.summary: Alleged that the Board improperly adopted remote participation by voting to adopt only 940 CMR 29.10(5).
allegations.key_passage: It is evident from the discussion that occurred prior to the Board's vote on February 13, 2013 that the Board's intent was to adopt the practice of remote participation as established by the whole of 940 CMR 29.10.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the Board failed to determine the cost of remote participation before adopting it, so it should be barred from using it.
allegations.key_passage: the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law regulations do not require that it state this information publicly at the time of adoption.

allegations.summary: Alleged that required statements about a remote participant were not made at the start of open and executive session at a March 2013 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: It is unclear whether the Board failed to make the statements, or simply failed to record in the minutes that it did so.

allegations.summary: Board's written responses called the complaints unfounded and violations de minimis; AG expressed concern but this is not a finding on an allegation.
allegations.key_passage: Any failure to follow the law's requirements undermines the goal of transparency.

remedy: Board members now serving must attend an Open Meeting Law training by an approved attorney or organization, or view the AG's online training video.
All Board members must certify to the AG's office within thirty (30) days after receiving the determination that they attended a live training or reviewed the video.
